title: Comodules, Matrix Coefficients, and Coalgebra Duality

items.title: Right comodules, comodule maps, and subcomodules
items.statement: Define a right comodule over a k-coalgebra C by a coaction ρ:M→M⊗C satisfying coassociativity and the counit law. Define comodule maps and embedded subcomodules.
items.strategy: State the right coaction equations with the fixed k-linear tensor convention; define subcomodules through injective comodule maps so no unproved tensor-inclusion assumption is hidden.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
William Chin, A Brief Introduction to Coalgebra Representation Theory

items.title: The dual convolution algebra and rational modules
items.statement: Define the convolution product on C*=Hom_k(C,k) by (f*g)(c)=(f⊗g)(Δ(c)) with unit ε. Define a left C*-module to be rational when each vector's orbit map is represented by a finite tensor in M⊗C under evaluation.
items.strategy: Fix the convolution and left-module side conventions; define rationality by finite-tensor orbit representation and defer naming its coaction until existence and uniqueness are proved.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
Andrew Baker, Hopf algebras over fields: an introduction, SMSTC supplementary course notes 2026–7

items.title: Kernels, images, quotients, and matrix coefficients of comodules
items.statement: Under AC, kernels, images and quotients of comodule maps inherit comodule structures and the first isomorphism theorem holds. The regular comodule exists. For a finite-dimensional comodule, its basis coefficients satisfy the comatrix identities, and any matrix satisfying those identities defines a comodule.
items.strategy: Use the tensor-kernel and injection facts to construct induced coactions, then compare coefficients in a finite basis and verify both directions of the matrix formula.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
William Chin, A Brief Introduction to Coalgebra Representation Theory

items.title: Every comodule element lies in a finite-dimensional subcomodule
items.statement: Assuming AC, every element of every right comodule over a k-coalgebra is contained in a finite-dimensional subcomodule. If C is finite-dimensional, the proof has a separate choice-free branch.
items.strategy: Expand ρ(m) with independent coalgebra coefficients, apply coassociativity and coefficient separation to the quotient by their first factors, then use the counit.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
William Chin, A Brief Introduction to Coalgebra Representation Theory

items.title: Right comodules are rational modules over the dual algebra
items.statement: Assuming AC, right C-comodules and their maps correspond to rational left C*-modules and their maps. For finite-dimensional C every left C*-module is rational by a choice-free finite-dual argument; no assertion is made that every module is rational for arbitrary C.
items.strategy: Verify the convolution algebra and the coaction action, reconstruct the unique coaction from each rational orbit tensor, and prove its axioms and morphism correspondence by finite-tensor separation.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
William Chin, A Brief Introduction to Coalgebra Representation Theory

items.title: Finite-dimensional algebra-coalgebra duality
items.statement: Finite-dimensional unital associative k-algebras dualize contravariantly to finite-dimensional coalgebras, and coalgebras dualize contravariantly to algebras. The finite-dimensional subcategories are equivalent under full linear duality and canonical bidual maps; the full dual construction is not asserted for infinite-dimensional algebras.
items.strategy: Transpose multiplication and unit using finite tensor duality, check coalgebra laws and map reversal by evaluation, and identify each finite object with its bidual.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
Andrew Baker, Hopf algebras over fields: an introduction, SMSTC supplementary course notes 2026–7

title: Comodules, Matrix Coefficients, and Coalgebra Duality — Examples

items.title: Group-graded vector spaces as comodules over the group-like coalgebra
items.statement: For any group G, the coalgebra with basis [g], Δ([g])=[g]⊗[g] and ε([g])=1 has right comodules exactly the G-graded vector spaces; the group law is unused by this coalgebra structure.
items.strategy: Check the group-like coalgebra axioms, define coaction on homogeneous vectors, and recover each grading component with finite coordinate functionals.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
William Chin, A Brief Introduction to Coalgebra Representation Theory

items.title: An infinite-dimensional dual algebra with a nonrational module
items.statement: For the infinite direct-sum group-like coalgebra C with countably many basis elements, the regular left C*-module C* is not rational and is not induced by a right C-comodule.
items.strategy: Its unit has orbit map f↦f, with infinite-dimensional image; each finite tensor in C*⊗C yields an orbit map with finite-dimensional image.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
Andrew Baker, Hopf algebras over fields: an introduction, SMSTC supplementary course notes 2026–7

items.title: A two-dimensional comodule and its coefficient matrix
items.statement: The standard two-dimensional comodule of the 2×2 comatrix coalgebra has coefficient matrix (c_ij), and its coaction identities reproduce Δ(c_ij)=Σ_l c_il⊗c_lj and ε(c_ij)=δ_ij.
items.strategy: Apply the coaction to each basis vector and compare both composites, retaining the ordered coefficient indices.

references.title: Daniel Kongsgaard and UCSD Math 207A, Hopf Algebras Lecture Notes, Spring 2020
William Chin, A Brief Introduction to Coalgebra Representation Theory
